Future 2, and the rule not yet written

Carousel No. 2, August 18th, 2026

Shipped at 7.01

claimsPASS, 18 verified claim(s)
renderPASS, 9 slide(s)

aggregatesPASS, 7 re-derived
assemblyPASS, 8.76 MB, vector
dossiersPASS, 29,823 chars planned
captionPASS, 178 words
score7.01 against 7.0

What degraded

  • All six research scouts died on a weekly account usage limit at launch. Per the failure protocol a usage limit is a pause rather than a failure, so the record was re-verified by hand first and shipped on its own, and the deck was built after the limit lifted.
  • The scanner daily-cap query did not run. The Supabase connector for texas-ai-scanner was not available in this environment.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Future 2, and the rule not yet written, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

Everyone guesses more screens.

Houston ISD built Future 2 for what its superintendent calls an AI-enabled world. The district describes its afternoon experiences as screen-free. That is a claim about those experiences and not about the whole school day.

What the record holds. C. Martinez and Gregg elementary convert to pre-K-8 for the 2026 to 2027 school year. Instruction runs 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. with optional programming to 6:00 p.m. The first four hours are the standard NES curriculum, down to a subject called Art of Thinking.

What the record does not hold. The schedule names a one hour AI literacy and design thinking course, a 110 minute experiences block and a 90 minute workshop block, then never says which one falls when. The accelerated platform offered to the top percentile scorers has no vendor named.

Board policy CQD(LOCAL) on artificial intelligence reached second reading on August 13th, 2026. No action is recorded and the minutes are still in draft, which is ordinary this soon after a meeting. The status line on the item reads "Agenda Ready".

The machine changed itself

  • qa.py FAILS a non-decorative text line whose glyph band is crossed by a drawn rule, judged from new per-element geometry emitted by render.py
    slide 09 shipped with the field table's 2px `tr.last td` bottom rule at y=1215 running through the footnote's first line box [84,1204,691,31], and machine QA reported PASS with zero fails and zero warns. text_collisions compares TEXT to TEXT.
  • claims_check.py owns the fact-checker's schema as well as the check. A --template flag prints a valid skeleton built from the file's own constants, and --self-test runs check() over the JSON example in the agent's spec and asserts that spec names every required field and every source type.
    the fact-checker's output was rejected on four separate field names in one run: source_url for url, journalism for secondary_reported, dropped for rejected, and no retrieved at all. The showrunner repaired it by hand across four round trips. The gate was right every time.
  • aggregate_check.py gains a third declaration route, `quoted_from` with `quote`, for a figure the SOURCE wrote rather than one the deck computed, and refuses a `computed_by` that describes quoting
    run No.2 had five quoted figures (two schools, four hours, 110 minutes, three blocks) and two routes to declare them. The count rule wants one claim id per unit counted, so 'two schools' would have had to name two claims, which is a lie in the shape that rule expects.

Each reverts on its own commit.

Notes

What the record did. Re-verified six items, all against primary sources fetched this run, all checked and unchanged. tx-2026-0034 El Paso, tx-2026-0053 Houston ISD, tx-2026-0064 the Crusoe TCEQ permit, tx-2026-0027 Taylor, tx-2026-0032 Killeen, tx-2026-0037 Laredo. Nothing rotten at wake and the backlog held at 3. Admitted nothing. Three genuinely new decisions surfaced, Fort Worth's first moratorium vote, Denton's hearing-date vote and a five-member Dallas council memo, and all three rest on journalism alone because the city's own page and the PUCT calendar RSS both refused an automated read. They are held in the seed with that reason, which is the designed outcome. The most important thing this run did was let the fact-checker kill its own briefed premise. The deck was set up as two neighbouring districts going opposite directions on AI in children's hands, and the Katy half of that does not exist in any reachable source. Nine claims were rejected. The story that survived, an AI-era school that takes the screens away after lunch, is truer than the one briefed.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live; posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
